newsitem.title: USA: Salomon Q2 global investment bank revs down.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Q2 global investment bank revs down.

text.p: Salomon Inc said Thursday its global investment banking revenues were $221 million, essentially unchanged from the 1997 first quarter but down from the record revenues of $251 million in the second quarter of 1996.
Salomon reported second-quarter net income of $1.77 a share, fully diluted, versus $2.34 a share, in the same period a year earlier.
The company said advisory and debt underwriting revenues were below the record level of last year's second quarter.
Equity sales/trading revenues fell to $229 million from $268 million. Salomon said equity sales and trading results continued at a level well above the quarterly average for 1996.
"The company experienced a very solid second quarter performance as a result of the contributions of many different business units," said chief executive Robert Denham.

Net revenues from commodities trading activities were $91 million for the second quarter of 1997, compared with negative revenues of $18 million in the year ago quarter. Commodities trading activities are conducted by its Phibro Inc unit.

Fixed income sales and trading net revenues fell to $532 million in the second quarter from $706 million in the second quarter of 1996. The company said the decrease reflects lower revenues in both proprietary trading and customer sales and trading "compared with the very strong results of the second quarter of 1996."
Asset management revenues were $20 million for the second quarter of 1997, nearly double the $11 million recorded in the second quarter of 1996, Salomon said.

Salomon said consolidated compensation and employee-related expenses for the three-month and six-month periods were $546 million and $1.111 billion, respectively, compared with $546 million and $1.096 billion in the three and six month periods ended June 30, 1996.
Salomon said during the second quarter it repurchased 1.9 million common shares for treasury at an average price of $51.59 per share.
Salomon also said it completed the sale of Basis Petroleum to Valero Energy Corp on May 1. Basis is reflected as a discontinued operation in the 1996 periods.
